assessment_summary: Group Charter - submisison of a group project charter including group roles and norms.
Business Models - submission of partner's business business and operating models, and IS architecture.
Pitch to Partner - presentation of a compelling case for problem/ opportunity and a project plan.Collection of feedback from partner, academics, and peers.
Innovation Review - submission of Innovation scorecard (template) and infographic of solution idea, to ensure innovative and creative thinking is embedded in the final solution.
Project Progress and Q&A – individual presentation followed by Q&A by each member of the team on the project progress as well as insights and lessons learned on professional skills.
Group Report – detailed report clearly communicating the project background, approach, analyses,solution recommendation and implementation.
Boardroom Presentation and Q&A - presentation of the project work with focus on solution recommendation followed by Q&A.

Leadership and Professional Development – exploration, development, and reflection on leadership and professional skills through the development of a portfolio for job applications, career development, and workplace success (professional identity). Two assessments: 1) Personal Goals development plan, and 2) Goals Achievement final exam, which is a hurdle task - students must pass it in order to pass the unit. Failing the hurdle task results in a capped fail mark of 49 in the unit.

details.Prerequisites ?: Completion of 18 credit points of units towards the Digital Business or Business Information Systems specialisation (including INFS5002)

items.label: Overview paragraph 1
items.text: This unit bridges the gap between theory and practice by integrating the knowledge and key skills developed across the Digital Business or Business Information Systems specialisation. It provides students with a practical teamwork experience to identify, analyse, and solve contemporary problems by exploring the socio-technical ecosystem in which a digital business operates. This experiential learning opportunity enhances students’ career-readiness by consolidating their professional skills and ability to apply the Business Information Systems knowledge in authentic situations.

items.label: Learning outcome 1
items.text: LO1. Apply advanced principles and theories related to digital business and information systems in the context of an actual business organisation

items.label: Learning outcome 2
items.text: LO2. Analyse open-ended business scenarios and evaluate the implications of digital technologies for business

items.label: Learning outcome 3
items.text: LO3. Apply techniques for organisational and business process analyses to resolve an actual business problem

items.label: Learning outcome 4
items.text: LO4. Communicate in a professional and confident manner, both orally and in writing, with actual business professionals

items.label: Learning outcome 5
items.text: LO5. Apply team management concepts and theories to effectively work in, and manage, cross-functional teams

items.label: Learning outcome 6
items.text: LO6. Analyse and reflect critically on the ethical and social implications of digital business
